subject: Architecture
title: The Eiffel Tower: From Outrage to Icon
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on The Eiffel Tower: From Outrage to Icon.

hook.text: Three hundred artists signed a petition calling the Eiffel Tower a 'metal asparagus' and a disgrace.

buildup.text: Gustave Eiffel built it for the 1889 World's Fair using 18,038 iron pieces and 2.5 million rivets.

discovery.text: It was meant to be temporary — a 20-year permit. Radio antennas on top made it too useful to remove.

twist.text: Eiffel built a secret apartment at the top where he entertained guests like Thomas Edison.

climax.text: The tower that Paris hated became the most visited paid monument in the world.

punchline.text: They wanted it torn down. Now it defines the skyline.

quiz.question: Why wasn't the Eiffel Tower demolished after its permit expired?
options: The French government ran out of demolition funds
Radio antennas on top made it too useful to remove
Public opinion shifted before the permit expired

details.summary: When Gustave Eiffel's 324-meter iron tower was built for the 1889 World's Fair, 300 prominent Parisians signed a petition calling it a 'metal asparagus' that would disfigure Paris.
details.whyItMatters: The Eiffel Tower is history's best example of architecture despised at birth becoming universally beloved. It proves that public taste can be profoundly wrong in the moment.
takeaways: 324 meters tall, built for the 1889 World's Fair in Paris
300 prominent citizens signed a petition opposing it
Originally temporary, saved as a radio antenna, now beloved worldwide

faq.question: Why did Parisians hate the Eiffel Tower?
faq.answer: Prominent artists, writers, and architects felt the exposed iron structure was ugly and industrial — unsuitable for Paris's refined stone architecture. They called it a factory chimney and predicted it would shame the city.

faq.question: How long was the Eiffel Tower the world's tallest structure?
faq.answer: From 1889 until the Chrysler Building surpassed it in 1930 — 41 years. During those four decades it was not only the tallest building but the tallest structure of any kind ever built by humans, doubling the height of the previous record holder (the Washington Monument).
